text:
anika: thinking out loud — we need a pragmatic bid plan for mixed spot/preemptible fleets that tolerates bursty demand. ideas on capacity-first vs price-first and graceful degradation?

mike: agree. leaning capacity-optimized primary with small price-optimized spill pool. capacity first keeps tail latencies stable for SLO buckets.

sara: +1. how big are you thinking for the warm buffer? static nodes or % of fleet?

anika: proposal: warm buffer = max(3 nodes, 6% of region pool) for each region. warm nodes are small pinned jobs (no heavy eviction) so they start KV cache and can take traffic fast.

josh: sounds sensible. add staggered drain so we don't lose all warm in one eviction event. e.g. use random jitter on preemptible termination handler: 30-120s.

mike: for bidding: set a floor at ~70% of on-demand price for capacity pools (to avoid getting completely priced out) and let price-optimized pools bid aggressively down to 10-15% for low-priority background jobs.

sara: what about cross-region fallback? do we do immediate failover or queued spill? cross-region adds egress + latency cost.

anika: prefer local region spill first. only failover to remote when local capacity < 20% target AND job is latency-insensitive. Route policy:
- latency-sensitive: capacity-optimized in same region, degrade to smaller model variant before cross-region
- batch/async: price-optimized cross-region allowed

mike: also recommend node labeling + taints:
```
# example k8s taint for warm buffer
kubectl label nodes warm-001 spot-warm=true
kubectl taint nodes warm-001 spot-warm=true:NoSchedule
```
that prevents user pods from accidentally landing.

josh: interruption handler flow idea: 1) cloud signal -> 2) infra-bot posts notice in channel and to /ops alert -> 3) mark node Unavailable in scheduler -> 4) trigger graceful drain with 5m grace then force. Add KV cache sync to S3 prior to evict.

infra-bot: incident notice template: "Preemptible eviction warning: region=us-west1, pool=capacity-optimized, eta=120s". Posting will include current warm-buffer count and suggestion to spin 1-2 on-demand fallback nodes.

sara: terraform snippet for GCP preemptible instance group? would help for ops runbook.

anika: here's a minimal example to pin a mixed pool (keep in runbook):
```
resource "google_compute_instance_template" "spot_template" {
  name_prefix = "spot-rt"
  scheduling {
    preemptible = true
    automatic_restart = false
  }
  labels = { pool = "price-optimized" }
}

resource "google_compute_region_instance_group_manager" "spot_pool" {
  name = "spot-pool"
  distribution_policy { }
  update_strategy = "ROLLING_UPDATE"
  version { instance_template = google_compute_instance_template.spot_template.self_link }
}
```

mike: ops checklist additions:
- monitor spot eviction rate per region
- alert if warm-buffer < configured threshold
- automated scaler to convert price-optimized -> capacity-optimized when eviction rate spikes

josh: on the scaler: add hysteresis, e.g. only convert if eviction rate > 5% sustained for 10m, and convert at most 1 pool per 30m to avoid flip-flop.

sara: cost modeling question: do we assume on-demand fallback will be used often? need to run sims with 50/30/20 split (capacity/price/on-demand) and stress synthetic load with poisson bursts.

anika: yes run sims. I'll spin up a small test cluster and run stress tests next week. plan: 2h run per region, synthetic 99th percentile latency target 350ms. please add any edge cases to test matrix.

mike: edge cases: simultaneous regional market crash, short TTL churn, instance-type specific interruptions (A100 vs H100), and egress throttling in cross-region failover.

josh: note for engineers: add a preemptible-drain hook that emits a KV checkpoint so model caches warm up faster on new nodes.

anika: thanks all — I'll draft a short runbook and post PR. linking to related notes: https://internal.redwood.ai/runbooks/spot-mix-play

sara: :thumbsup:

mike: :+1:

infra-bot: action created: "spot-warm-buffer-sim" assigned to @anika, due 3d.
